title: refute — the refuter's verdict contract
description: The refuter's output for ADR 0016. Every shape check in review-merge's refute_gate first jq program becomes a rule here; the verdict itself (pass only when every criterion is met and there are no defects) is computed by refute_gate and is NOT expressible as a schema, so it stays in the gate. A valid Input receipt proves this schema passed (submit stamped _io). _io is stamped by the server and is not part of this schema.

summary.description: Two or three sentences: what you checked and what you found.

criteria.description: The requirements of the closed issues (or the PR description when there are none), one entry each.

items.description: One requirement and how it was tested.

criterion.description: The requirement, quoted or closely paraphrased, in one sentence.

status.description: met: you can cite the file:line that implements it and found nothing contradicting it. not_met: missing, partly done, or contradicted by the code. unverifiable: you cannot tell from the code and the diff; say what evidence is missing.

evidence.description: path/to/file.py:42 and what it shows, or what is missing and where you looked.

defects.description: What a careful maintainer would refuse to merge. Empty when none found.

items.description: A concrete wrong behavior, crash, lost data, security hole, broken public contract, or a test weakened so it no longer tests the behavior.

file.description: The repository-relative path where the defect is.

line.description: The line of the defect, or null when it has no single line.

scenario.description: One sentence: the concrete input or state, and the wrong result it produces.
